transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (PM), Lucia Gomez (Eng Manager), Ethan Park (SRE), Diego Alvarez (Infra), Maya Chen (Product Ops), Ravi Singh (Tech Lead)

Summary:
Quick postmortem / launch-readiness sync after last weekend's incident that increased latencies for the Redwood-hosted route. We walk through timeline, root cause (autoscaler misconfiguration + cold KV cache behavior under burst), mitigations applied, and next steps to be launch-ready for the Q4 rollout.

Topics covered: incident timeline, autoscaler policy, capacity sigs, KV cache warmup strategies, benchmark gaps, security/compliance gating, canary strategy.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Samir: okay, let's get started, thanks everyone for carving out time, this is the postmortem + launch readiness check for the Q4 feature rollout. we ran into increased P95 last saturday, called a brief incident, diego took lead on the mitigation, thanks for that.
[00:00:22] Diego: yeah no problem, uh quick note, the mitigation was mostly to add temporary manual capacity and bump some autoscaler params, that got latency back to normal but we need a permanent fix.
[00:00:35] Lucia: can we walk through the timeline? i have some notes but might be missing a piece around the KV cache behavior.
[00:00:45] Ethan: timeline — about 02:10 UTC we started seeing queue growth on our front pods, kv-cache miss rate spiked, batching didn't help because new sessions were cold, autoscaler kicked but the min buffer was too low so it scaled slower than request ramp.
[00:01:10] Ravi: just to be clear, the model variant we were running was the quantized 13B that has a longer cold startup on the infra path; so kernel selection + cuda context warmup added 200-400ms per cold replica during the tight ramp.
[00:01:35] Samir: so root cause is twofold — autoscaler tuning and cold-replica startup combined with prefix/KV cache cold misses. would you all agree?
[00:01:48] Lucia: yes, and i want to stress the prefix cache warm-up. our cache warming heuristic didn't prefetch for certain test users, and that meant the first 100 requests per pod hit the backend hot path.
[00:02:02] Diego: also, the autoscaler threshold used the 60s average CPU metric, whereas we should be looking at a shorter-timescale QPS estimator for these bursts. the policy file had a node buffer of 0.05 which is too small.
[00:02:20] Ethan: the alerts also didn't correlate queue length with kv cache miss spikes, so the SRE runbook raised the ticket later than ideal. we need composite alerts.
[00:02:35] Maya: from product ops, the downstream impact was that a small percentage of users saw latency > 2.5s which caused error budget burn for that route. execs want a crisp timeline and proof we won't repeat on rollout.
[00:02:52] Samir: understood. let's go over fixes that got us stable and then permanent mitigations. diego, can you summarize the immediate mitigation?
[00:03:05] Diego: immediate: we manually increased replica count and spun a warm pool in the region, added a node group temporarily, and applied a patched autoscaler with a quicker scale-up target; that reduced queue and latencies within ~5 minutes.
[00:03:20] Ravi: and i ran a quick benchmark of token throughput once we had warm replicas, results matched expected throughput but the cold-replica penalty was measurable — plan to measure that more formally.
[00:03:33] Samir: permanent mitigations?
[00:03:36] Diego: update autoscaler policy — add min buffer of 10% of peak capacity for routes marked as low-latency critical, switch metric to a short-window QPS based estimator, lower cooldown for scale-up.
[00:03:52] Ethan: SRE will add composite alerts: (queue_length > X AND kv_cache_miss_rate > Y) AND latency P95 > Z; also add runbook step to pre-warm pools when deploys change model variants.
[00:04:10] Lucia: engineering to add a KV cache warmup step to rollout pipeline — pre-populate from recent prefixes or synthetic prompts during canary; also add a small cache-warmup window prior to directing 100% traffic.
[00:04:28] Maya: ops will update the launch readiness checklist to make the warmup and autoscaler checks gating requirements for go/no-go.
[00:04:40] Samir: good. what are the risks if we don't do these before canary?
[00:04:45] Ravi: user-visible latency spikes on first ramp, error budget burn, higher token cost per successful request while we spin up new replicas, and potential customer tickets which is bad for PLG motion.
[00:04:58] Diego: also risk of cascading scale — if cold replicas cause CPU spikes, autoscaler may thrash if thresholds not tuned.
[00:05:10] Lucia: a quick question — is there any security/compliance work that could block rolling out the warm pool approach? KMS/HSM keys for private deployments?
[00:05:22] Maya: there is one gating item: for Private/VPC customers we need to ensure warm pool images don't leak ephemeral keys and that we rotate any in-memory tokens. we'll update the runbook to scrub secrets and use instance profiles.
[00:05:36] Ethan: on monitoring, we should instrument KV cache hit latency separately from model token latency so we can triage faster.
[00:05:46] Samir: agreed. okay let's step into the benchmark gaps — ravi you mentioned more formal numbers.
[00:05:52] Ravi: right, current benchmarks simulate steady-state throughput but not sudden spikes with high new-session ratios; i'll add a spike workload that mimics our PLG signup test and measure cold replica penalty across 3 GPU types (A100/H100 and an NPU variant) and include quantized vs fp16 variants.
[00:06:15] Lucia: please include different sequence lengths, the kernel selection changes with long sequences and we saw weird perf on >1024 tokens.
[00:06:24] Ravi: will do.
[00:06:28] Diego: one more infra note — the kernel selection path sometimes falls back to a non-optimal path when memory is tight; that's a separate perf bug but it exacerbates cold-start. opening ticket.
[00:06:41] Samir: ok let's talk schedule — we want to be ready to start canary on 2026-10-12. does that still feel achievable if we complete the listed action items?
[00:06:54] Lucia: yes, provided we get the autoscaler patch and bake the warm pool in staging by 2026-10-08, and the perf numbers confirm no regressions.
[00:07:03] Maya: i'll block exec update for 2026-10-09 to show the gating checklist and artifacts.
[00:07:10] Ethan: i'll run the DR drill with a simulated node loss during canary to ensure fallback policies are sane.
[00:07:18] Samir: good. any follow-ups on security/compliance beyond the warm-pool secret handling?
[00:07:25] Maya: we need to attach SOC2 evidence of drift checks and ensure RBAC roles for canary operators are correct; I'll draft the evidence pack.
[00:07:34] Ravi: quick thought — could we improve cost by using a small cache of smaller instances to handle warm traffic and only use big GPUs for heavy tokens? that's a bigger architecture discussion but maybe worth noting.
[00:07:48] Diego: that's an interesting cost/playoff trade; might introduce additional routing complexity and KV cache coherence concerns. flag for next architecture sync.
[00:07:59] Samir: ok, let's capture that as a backlog item.
[00:08:03] Maya: final recap before we close, i'll read next steps: diego will push autoscaler patch and run soak, ravi will re-run perf, ethan will update alerts and runbook, lucia will add warmup to pipeline, samir will finalize canary plan and comms. everyone?
[00:08:22] Lucia: yes.
[00:08:24] Ethan: yep.
[00:08:26] Diego: done.
[00:08:28] Ravi: yep.
[00:08:30] Maya: great.
[00:08:32] Samir: thanks all, i'll send the postmortem note and updated checklist after this meeting. meet adjourned.
